name: Masakhane
summary: Masakhane is a grassroots research community that builds NLP resources for African languages, led by African researchers. Its Hugging Face org hosts hundreds of models and a set of benchmark datasets, and its code lives on GitHub.

notable_releases.name: AfriMGSM
notable_releases.note: Math reasoning benchmark for African languages

notable_releases.name: AfriMMLU
notable_releases.note: Multi-task knowledge benchmark for African languages

openness: Models, datasets and code are published openly on Hugging Face and GitHub; licences vary per resource.

contributions.title: Participatory research model
contributions.note: Brings volunteers from across Africa together to build machine translation and other NLP resources for their own languages.

contributions.title: Open benchmarks
contributions.note: Publishes evaluation datasets such as AfriMGSM, AfriMMLU and MasakhaNEWS for African languages.

contributions.title: Named entity recognition
contributions.note: Created MasakhaNER, a named entity dataset covering several African languages.

github_highlights.name: masakhane-ner
github_highlights.note: Named entity recognition for African languages

papers.title: Participatory Research for Low-resourced Machine Translation: A Case Study in African Languages
MasakhaNER: Named Entity Recognition for African Languages

contact_note: The website lists a leadership group mailing list; the GitHub community repo explains how to join.

name: Lelapa AI
summary: Lelapa AI is a South African startup building language AI for African languages, including a commercial speech and translation product called Vulavula. It also releases research models and datasets openly, notably InkubaLM.

notable_releases.name: InkubaLM-0.4B
notable_releases.note: Small language model for African languages

openness: Research models and datasets are on Hugging Face (InkubaLM-0.4B is listed under CC BY-NC 4.0); the commercial Vulavula product is closed.

contributions.title: InkubaLM
contributions.note: Released a small open language model aimed at several African languages.

contributions.title: Open datasets
contributions.note: Published instruction, monolingual and isiXhosa speech datasets.

contributions.title: Commercial speech and translation
contributions.note: Sells Vulavula, a speech-to-text and translation product with code-switching support.

papers.title: InkubaLM: A small language model for low-resource African languages

contact_note: Only a careers address is printed on the site; LinkedIn and X are linked.

name: Ghana NLP
summary: Ghana NLP is an open-source initiative working on NLP for Ghanaian languages and applications to local problems. It publishes Twi and other language models and parallel text datasets on Hugging Face and code on GitHub.
openness: Models and datasets are published on Hugging Face and code on GitHub; licences differ per resource.

contributions.title: Twi language models
contributions.note: Trained and released BERT-style models for Akuapem and Asante Twi.

contributions.title: Parallel corpora
contributions.note: Published English parallel text for several Ghanaian languages.

contributions.title: Translation systems
contributions.note: Built Twi translation work and evaluations of LLMs on Ghanaian languages.

github_highlights.name: nsanku
github_highlights.note: Zero-shot translation evaluation for Ghanaian languages

contact_note: Reach via the website or LinkedIn; no organisation email seen on the homepage.

name: Zindi
summary: Zindi runs a data science competition platform and community for African AI builders. Its GitHub organisation holds collected challenge solutions; its own Hugging Face org has no public models.
openness: Open code for challenge solutions on GitHub; competition data is governed by each challenge's terms, so it is only partly open. Borderline inclusion.

contributions.title: Competition platform
contributions.note: Hosts machine learning challenges for African problems with a large community.

contributions.title: Shared solutions
contributions.note: Collects solutions to challenges in public GitHub repos.

contributions.title: Partnership datasets
contributions.note: Challenges have supported projects such as InkubaLM notebooks (seen on Lelapa's GitHub).

name: Deep Learning Indaba
summary: Deep Learning Indaba strengthens machine learning in Africa through an annual conference, schools and community programmes, run by a non-profit company registered in the UK. Its GitHub organisation publishes open practical notebooks from each Indaba.
openness: Teaching notebooks are open on GitHub; it does not train large models. Borderline inclusion as an education and community body.

contributions.title: Annual Indaba
contributions.note: Runs the Deep Learning Indaba gathering for African machine learning researchers.

contributions.title: Open practicals
contributions.note: Publishes practical notebooks from each edition on GitHub.

contributions.title: Community building
contributions.note: Supports local IndabaX events and a non-profit structure registered with Companies House.

name: Digital Umuganda
summary: Digital Umuganda works on African language NLP, speech and data collection, with a focus on Kinyarwanda and other languages. Its Hugging Face org hosts speech models and the AfriVoice datasets.
openness: Models and datasets are public on Hugging Face; licences per repo. Only the Hugging Face org was opened, so website and legal form are unverified.

contributions.title: AfriVoice datasets
contributions.note: Releases speech datasets in languages such as Kinyarwanda and Swahili.

contributions.title: Speech models
contributions.note: Publishes ASR and TTS models for Kinyarwanda and Lingala.

contributions.title: Data collection
contributions.note: Described as a data-collection group for African NLP.

contact_note: Via the Hugging Face org page.

name: Crane AI Labs
summary: Crane AI Labs describes itself as building culturally relevant AI for the Global South. Its Hugging Face org hosts Swahili and Luganda Gemma-based models, tokenizers and benchmark datasets.
openness: Models and datasets are public on Hugging Face; base models carry their upstream licence terms. Country comes from press coverage, not the org page.

contributions.title: Swahili and Luganda models
contributions.note: Fine-tuned small models for East African languages.

contributions.title: Datasets
contributions.note: Released evaluation and speech-related datasets for Luganda.

contributions.title: Offline use
contributions.note: Provides GGUF and LiteRT versions for local use.

contact_note: Via the Hugging Face org page.

name: Latam-GPT (CENIA)
summary: Latam-GPT is a Latin American language model project coordinated by CENIA, Chile's national AI centre. It publishes models, a regional text corpus, benchmarks and data-curation tools openly.
openness: Weights, corpus and tools are public on Hugging Face and GitHub; the SFT model carries a Llama 3.1 licence and the corpus a custom licence.

contributions.title: Regional corpus
contributions.note: Released a Latin American text corpus and a research variant.

contributions.title: Fine-tuned model
contributions.note: Published an instruction-tuned 70B model built on Llama 3.1.

contributions.title: Data tooling
contributions.note: Open tools for language ID, toxicity classification and LLM-aided filtering.

contact_note: Email printed on latamgpt.org; CENIA also lists info@cenia.cl.

name: Maritaca AI
summary: Maritaca AI is a Brazilian startup behind the Sabiá language models and the MariTalk API, built for Portuguese. It releases some open weights and several Portuguese benchmarks while its flagship models are served commercially.
openness: Some weights (S5-nano) are open under Apache 2.0; larger commercial models are API-only. City is approximate and unverified.

contributions.title: Sabiá models
contributions.note: Developed Portuguese-focused language models, with early versions released openly.

contributions.title: Benchmarks
contributions.note: Published Portuguese evaluation sets such as ENEM and OAB-Bench.

contributions.title: Bias evaluation
contributions.note: Released a multi-turn bias benchmark.

papers.title: Sabiá: Portuguese Large Language Models

name: Polygl0t (Tucano)
summary: Polygl0t develops open foundation models for low-resource languages, best known for the Tucano family of Portuguese models. It publishes weights, corpora such as GigaVerbo, and training code; the project is linked to the University of Bonn.
openness: Weights (Apache 2.0 on the instruct model checked), datasets and code are public on Hugging Face and GitHub. Brazilian focus but based in Germany.

contributions.title: Tucano models
contributions.note: Open Portuguese language models trained end to end in the language.

contributions.title: GigaVerbo
contributions.note: Large open Portuguese text corpora in several versions.

contributions.title: Training code
contributions.note: Open llm-foundry for training and evaluating models.

papers.title: Tucano: Advancing Neural Text Generation for Portuguese
Tucano 2 Cool: Better Open Source LLMs for Portuguese

name: SomosNLP
summary: SomosNLP is an international community of Spanish speakers working on NLP, running yearly hackathons and building open Spanish datasets and models. City is a placeholder because the community is distributed.
openness: Datasets, models, course material and website are open on Hugging Face and GitHub.

contributions.title: Hackathons
contributions.note: Runs annual community hackathons that produce Spanish and regional datasets and models.

contributions.title: Open datasets
contributions.note: Hosts datasets such as SMC and RecetasDeLaAbuela.

contributions.title: Education
contributions.note: Maintains a practical NLP course and a corpus list.

discord_note: Public Discord for the Spanish NLP community.
contact_note: Join the Discord linked on the website.

name: Te Hiku Media
summary: Te Hiku Media is a Māori iwi media organisation in Kaitaia that builds te reo Māori speech technology under Māori data sovereignty. Its code and a data-sovereignty licence are public on GitHub; some data and models are governed by that licence rather than open licences.
openness: Code and corpora on GitHub; data held under Māori data sovereignty principles, so openness is conditional. Hugging Face presence not found. Borderline inclusion.

contributions.title: Māori speech recognition
contributions.note: Built te reo Māori speech tools with community-contributed recordings.

contributions.title: Kaitiakitanga License
contributions.note: Authored a licence for data held under Māori guardianship.

contributions.title: Public APIs and demos
contributions.note: Provides Kōrero Māori API demos and open repos.

contact_note: Email printed on the website footer.

name: JoeyLLM
summary: JoeyLLM, formerly Southern Cross AI, is a developer-led initiative to build an Australian open-source language model. So far its Hugging Face org lists country-focused datasets, and its GitHub holds interface and team repos.
openness: Datasets are public; no model weights were listed on the Hugging Face org when checked. Early-stage.

contributions.title: Australian dataset
contributions.note: Published a roughly 1B-token Australian dataset.

contributions.title: Country datasets
contributions.note: Also published UK, New Zealand and Canada datasets.

contributions.title: Chat demo
contributions.note: Maintains a chat interface repo.

name: Maincode
summary: Maincode is a Melbourne AI company that describes itself as independent and runs its own hardware. It has released some models on Hugging Face, including Maincoder-1B and Matilda base models, while its main Matilda product is not open-weight.
openness: Selected models are open on Hugging Face; the commercial flagship is not. Borderline inclusion.

contributions.title: Maincoder-1B
contributions.note: Open small coding model.

contributions.title: Matilda base models
contributions.note: Published base models at several sizes.

contributions.title: Local infrastructure
contributions.note: Trains and serves models on hardware it owns in Melbourne.

name: BigScience
summary: BigScience was a year-long open research workshop that produced the BLOOM multilingual language model and many related datasets and tools. Hosting is on Hugging Face, and the project is now mainly an archive. City is a placeholder for a distributed collaboration.
openness: Open weights, datasets and code, with BLOOM under the Responsible AI License.

contributions.title: BLOOM
contributions.note: Released a 176B multilingual open-access model.

contributions.title: Prompts and datasets
contributions.note: Built P3, xP3 and promptsource.

contributions.title: Distributed LLMs
contributions.note: Created Petals for collaborative inference and fine-tuning.

papers.title: BLOOM: A 176B-Parameter Open-Access Multilingual Language Model
Petals: Collaborative Inference and Fine-tuning of Large Models

name: BigCode
summary: BigCode is an open scientific collaboration, run by Hugging Face and ServiceNow Research, on code language models. It released the StarCoder models, The Stack datasets and evaluation tools. Independence is partial because two companies host it.
openness: Open weights under the BigCode OpenRAIL-M family, with datasets and code public.

contributions.title: StarCoder models
contributions.note: Open code LLMs trained on permissively licensed code.

contributions.title: The Stack
contributions.note: Large open code datasets with opt-out.

contributions.title: Benchmarks
contributions.note: BigCodeBench and an evaluation harness.

papers.title: StarCoder: may the source be with you!
StarCoder 2 and The Stack v2: The Next Generation

name: LAION (incl. OpenAssistant)
summary: LAION is a non-profit making datasets, tools and models openly available for research. It also co-organised the OpenAssistant crowd-sourced conversation project.
openness: Datasets, models and code are open with mixed licences.

contributions.title: LAION-5B
contributions.note: Released an open large-scale image-text dataset.

OpenAssistant Conversations -- Democratizing Large Language Model Alignment

name: MLCommons
summary: MLCommons is a consortium that publishes ML benchmarks (MLPerf), datasets and metadata standards. Its GitHub hosts reference implementations; Hugging Face hosts datasets such as People's Speech. The website returned a bot check when opened.
openness: Open code and datasets; licences vary.

name: Axolotl AI
summary: Axolotl AI maintains the open-source Axolotl fine-tuning framework used by many open model builders. Code and small models are public.

name: Open Language Data Initiative (OLDI)
summary: OLDI is a community effort on open multilingual NLP data for underserved languages, maintaining FLORES+ and the OLDI Seed machine translation data.
openness: Datasets and code are public on Hugging Face and GitHub.

contributions.title: Resource list
